purpose: Review Step 46 by adding the missing curvature-block invariance calculation.
main_principle: At an orbifold fixed point, the Einstein curvature blocks R^± commute with the local isotropy action. Therefore the traceless Weyl block W^± lies in Sym^2_0(R^3)^G for the chiral block on which Gamma acts through G=Gamma/{±1}<SO(3). This is the same spin-2 invariant representation as the l=2 harmonic computation.

k\u00e4hler_orientation_caution.standard_complex_Kleinian_convention: For a local complex/ADE quotient Gamma<SU(2) preserving the hyperkähler triple, Gamma acts trivially on the Kähler self-dual block and by the adjoint action on the opposite block. If a note uses the opposite SU(2)_L/R naming, plus/minus labels must be swapped.
k\u00e4hler_orientation_caution.positive_KE_pinned_block: In complex orientation, R_+ = diag(Lambda,0,0). This nonzero traceless Weyl block can occur only in the chiral block on which the isotropy action is trivial or at least has the needed invariant direction.
k\u00e4hler_orientation_caution.E_type_review: For E6/E7/E8, the nontrivial isotropy block has W=0 and R=(Lambda/3)I, hence is invertible for Lambda>0. Thus E-type is not an extra double-degeneracy loophole for reversed bubbles in a positive KE limit; depending on convention it either obstructs the opposite block or would make the claimed KE orientation impossible.

review_conclusion: The word 'generic' should be removed from Step 46. The sequence supplies a fixed orbifold limit; the honest statement is a finite set of degeneracy alternatives at its singular points and gluing directions.
For A1, Gamma/{±1} is trivial and both chiral blocks are unconstrained by isotropy; this is the main double-degeneracy locus exemplified by the bi-Kähler product quotient.
For A_k (k>=2) and D_k the degeneracy condition lives in a 1-, 2-, or 3-dimensional invariant curvature space and becomes explicit scalar equations in adapted coordinates.

For E-types the nontrivial block is scalar positive and cannot have a kernel for Lambda>0. Step 46's 'E-type compatible bubble locus' is therefore at least misframed and is not a KE loophole of the same kind as A1 double degeneracy.
